title: No predicate retry strategies for async code, and no way to combine them with the existing ones
text_original: Third and last PR after breaking down https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/433 (follows https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/437). After DRYing the `iter()` function and making `AsyncRetrying` support `async` callbacks, add new `async` strategies (basically a copy-paste) and improve typing. Release note: Added the ability to use async functions for retries. This way, you can now use asyncio coroutines for retry strategy predicates.
text_rewritten: The result and exception predicate strategies are the readable way to express a retry policy, but their predicates have to be ordinary functions. Ours need to await something — a feature-flag lookup and a shared cache — so on the asynchronous path we are forced down to a raw `retry=` callable and have to rediscover how to inspect the outcome by hand, and once we do that we can no longer use `|` or `&` to combine it with the ordinary exception-type strategy we already rely on. Please provide asynchronous counterparts of the predicate strategies in a `tenacity.asyncio.retry` module: `retry_if_result(predicate)` and `retry_if_exception(predicate)` taking coroutine predicates over the returned value and the raised exception respectively, plus `retry_any(*strategies)` and `retry_all(*strategies)`. Combining an existing synchronous strategy with one of the new asynchronous ones through `|` or `&` must produce something the asynchronous retry loop can evaluate, in either operand order. Combining two synchronous strategies has to keep working exactly as it does today.

Ours need to await something — a feature-flag lookup and a shared cache — so on the asynchronous path we are forced down to a raw `retry=` callable and have to rediscover how to inspect the outcome by hand, and once we do that we can no longer use `|` or `&` to combine it with the ordinary exception-type strategy we already rely on. Combining an existing synchronous strategy with one of the new asynchronous ones through `|` or `&` must produce something the asynchronous retry loop can evaluate, in either operand order. Combining two synchronous strategies has to keep working exactly as it does today.
acceptance_hint: `retry_if_result` and `retry_if_exception` from `tenacity.asyncio.retry` accept coroutine predicates and drive an asynchronous retried function correctly; a synchronous strategy combined with an asynchronous one through `|` produces a strategy the asynchronous loop evaluates; purely synchronous composition is unchanged.
